The dash needs a newer app
The dash needs a firmware update
Allow Nearby devices to connect to the dash
The dash doesn\'t know this phone any more. Forget sārathi in Bluetooth settings, then pair again
To connect to your sārathi dash over Bluetooth. The app only talks to the dash you pair; it never scans for other devices.
Android shows a small ongoing notification while the dash is connected, so you can see the link is running and stop it.
Navigation needs your position during the ride. It stays on this phone and the dash; the dash only ever gets it as distances from the start of the ride.
Your phone stays locked in your pocket for the whole ride. Choose \"Allow all the time\" so navigation keeps working with the screen off, and comes back by itself if Android restarts the app.
Let the app run without battery restrictions, so Android doesn\'t stop the link to the dash mid-ride. It uses little battery while connected.
Turn the dash on nearby. Pick \"sarathi\" in the list, then compare the 6-digit code on the phone and on the dash: if they match, turn the knob to Pair and click.
Turn on notification access for sārathi, so the dash can show what\'s playing and skip tracks. sārathi only reads the playing music; it doesn\'t read or keep other apps\' notifications.
See who\'s calling on the dash, and answer or reject with the knob. sārathi doesn\'t read your contacts or call log; the name comes from the call notification your phone already shows.
The dash\'s settings lock while the bike moves, judged from the phone\'s GPS speed.
\"Stopped below\" must stay under \"Moving from\". To lower \"Moving from\", lower \"Stopped below\" first; to raise \"Stopped below\", raise \"Moving from\" first.
Off: the dash\'s settings stay unlocked while riding.
The dash will let you change settings while you ride. Looking down and turning the knob at speed is dangerous: change settings only when you\'ve stopped.
Recorded for desk tests: replay it from Home.
Google routes aren\'t recorded: Google\'s terms limit keeping its content.

Ride started: the phone can go in your pocket, locked.
Used for searching places and for routes. If it can\'t be used (no key, over quota, no network), the next one in the fallback order takes over.
A different backend for search or for routing, and the order to fall back in.
Built into this app from files on the build computer; never shown, never sent anywhere but to their own service.
Google Navigation terms: not accepted yet. Google routes only after you accept them.
Counted on this phone. Google is blocked at 95 % of its free monthly allowance and warns at 80 %; Mappls stops for the day at its caps or when it reports a limit.
Debug builds. Fetches the map tiles around the phone at both levels and shows where each came from: online, the cache or the offline region.

Debug builds. Each route asked for fails one more backend, before any call: Google over quota, then Mappls, then OSM online, which leaves OSM offline. A simulated ride leaves the road to reroute through them. Off when the app restarts.
The default is FOSSGIS\'s public server: free for non-commercial use, at most one request a second.

The phone connects by itself when your dash is nearby and on, even locked in your pocket.
Keep the link alive on this phone
Nothing OS: Settings, Apps, sārathi, Battery: Unrestricted. Don\'t swipe the app away from Recents during a ride.
Samsung: Settings, Apps, sārathi, Battery: Unrestricted. Also Settings, Battery, Background usage limits: take sārathi off \"Sleeping apps\" and \"Deep sleeping apps\".
Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO: Settings, Apps, sārathi: Autostart on, Battery saver: No restrictions. In Recents, long-press sārathi and lock it.
OnePlus: Settings, Apps, sārathi, Battery: Unrestricted (or \"Allow background activity\"). In Recents, lock sārathi.
OPPO, realme: Settings, Apps, sārathi, Battery: allow background activity and auto launch. In Recents, lock sārathi.
vivo, iQOO: Settings, Battery, Background power consumption: allow sārathi. Settings, Apps, sārathi: Autostart on.
Huawei, Honor: Settings, Battery, App launch: sārathi to \"Manage manually\" with all three switches on.
Pixel: the Battery step above is enough.
If the link stops mid-ride, look for battery or background settings for sārathi on this phone and allow it to run unrestricted.
Off by default. After a ride, shows roads you rode that OpenStreetMap doesn\'t have yet, so you can add them with your own OpenStreetMap account.
On: %1$d ride(s), %2$.1f km recorded on this phone

While the dash is connected, sārathi records your ride's GPS track on this phone: satellite fixes only, while moving.

After a ride, never during it, the app shows places where you rode a road OpenStreetMap doesn't have. Nothing leaves this phone unless you choose it for one place:
• upload that part of your GPS track to OpenStreetMap: public, and linked to your account unless you pick trackable;
• add a public note for local mappers, in your words;
• add the road yourself, after you check it on a map.

Each is made with your own OpenStreetMap account and shown to you before it's sent. What goes to OpenStreetMap stays public for good. Places near where you start and stop, and your saved places, are cut from uploads.

Tracks are deleted after 30 days, or when you turn this off.
Turn off and delete the tracks?
The GPS tracks recorded on this phone are deleted. Nothing already sent to OpenStreetMap changes.
Places on your recent rides where OpenStreetMap has no road. Each is checked against OpenStreetMap as it is today before it shows here.

A minute either side of the place. Points near where you started and stopped, and near your saved places, are left out.

Trackable: not listed and not linked to you; the points and times are still public
